about: Reference data for parsec_python.Relaxation.lbfgsb, produced by the ORIGINAL Fortran
sources of PARSEC (lbfgsb.f = L-BFGS-B 3.0, linpack.f, timer.f) through a small driver
that calls setulb with the argument association of domove.f90.
The driver, its build script and the generator of this file are tools kept

reference_build.blas: netlib reference BLAS 3.12.0 (static libblas.a): sequential ddot

encoding: Keys ending in _b64 hold little-endian IEEE doubles in base64, split into chunks;
evaluation_points_b64 is the matrix (number of evaluations) x n, row after row.
tasks is the task string after every setulb call, in call order: the first call has
task = START, f and g are supplied whenever the task starts with FG.
Text files are stored as lists of lines exactly as the Fortran wrote them.
dsave(6:10) (CPU times) are set to zero in dsave_without_times_b64.

infinite_function_value.comment: the objective returns +Infinity for f at one evaluation (g is unchanged)

comment: relax_restart.dat round trips on one case.  fortran_dump is the file the Fortran driver
wrote, in the layout of domove.f90, when evaluation number before_evaluation was requested;
the run then went on, so the case itself is the uninterrupted reference.  The Python code
wrote its own file at the same point (python_dump_sha256 is the SHA-256 of that text with
LF line ends); the Fortran driver read it as domove.f90 reads relax_restart.dat and
continued: fortran_continuation_of_python_dump is what it did.
fortran_dump: Iteration number, number of movable atoms

comment: relax_restart.dat written by the Fortran PARSEC during a BFGS relaxation of a water
molecule (isolated, Grid_Spacing 0.3, Force_Min 0.02, 3 movable atoms, unrestricted
BFGS).  The file is stored as numbers; file_sha256 is the SHA-256 of its 23422 bytes.
Slots that L-BFGS-B never wrote hold whatever the Fortran allocate left there.
Short runs taken from a randomized comparison with the Fortran, chosen so that the
statements which the cases above do not execute are reached.  They are replayed: the
recorded f and g are supplied (evaluation_gradients_b64), so the objective may be any
function, also with inconsistent or non-finite values.  script has one letter per event:
C = call of setulb, E = evaluation, B = the caller replaces the bounds by lower2/upper2.
injected_tasks are task strings set by the caller before the call with that number.

comment: The Fortran routines dcstep and dcsrch called directly.  Reals are hexadecimal images
of IEEE doubles (most significant byte first).  dcstep: input is stx, fx, dx, sty, fy,
dy, stp, fp, dp, stpmin, stpmax; output is stx, fx, dx, sty, fy, dy, stp.  dcsrch: a
complete line search on the polynomial c0 + c1 s + ... + c4 s^4 (f = c0 and g = c1 on
the first call, task = START), one example for each final task; calls lists the task
and the step after every call.
